_comment: Which consumer each public capability must reach, so that "implemented" and "shipped" stop being the same word.
每个 public 能力必须到达哪一类消费者——这样「实现了」和「出货了」才不是同一句话。
Four classes, because they fail differently:
* `motor-owned` -- the library's own loop must contain it, so it has to be reachable from a production
translation unit under `src/`. Unreachable is a defect: the header exists, the tests are green, and a
user of the released package cannot get at it (`stall_start.hpp` was exactly this);
* `diagnostic` -- only useful if something can read it out, so each `abi` name must exist in the C surface;
* `contract` -- a port is a promise, and `stub` names the reference implementation that proves the promise
* `policy` -- composed by the host, so reachability from `src/` is *not* expected; what it owes instead is a
runnable example. `example: null` is allowed and counted, because "no example yet" and "we did not think
about it" must not look the same in a file;
* `todo` -- not decided yet. Counted every run against `todo_baseline`, which may only fall.
`known_unshipped` is the honest debt list: a `motor-owned` header that nothing in `src/` reaches, with the batch
that fixes it. It is a ratchet in both directions -- an entry whose header has become reachable is itself a
failure, because a stale exception hides the next real one.
This gate is the STATIC half of the rule. The dynamic half ("switch the thing off and the output must move")
is a test convention, not a gate: `blast` and `wired` both answer "is the wire there", neither answers "is the
thing on the other end right".

core/deadtime.hpp.why: the loss model is applied by the caller before modulating: `Svpwm` sees no phase currents, so this release has no production slot for it

core/friction_comp.hpp.why: a feed-forward the caller adds to its torque command; `Motor` has no compensation slot, which is why nothing in `src/` includes it

core/gear_ratio.hpp.why: a coordinate transform between the caller's units and the axis; by design it lives on the caller's side of the boundary

core/hall.hpp.why: there is no HAL input for the three pins yet (batch 1 adds one), so a host has to write its own reader even though the decoder ships

core/soft_limit.hpp.why: a limiter the caller applies to its own position commands; `Motor` takes commands already limited

core/trace.hpp.why: the recorder is only useful if something can read it out, so its reachability is the C ABI shape of it

hal/clock.hpp.why: a port is only a contract until something implements it; the stub is what proves the shape is implementable

hal/current_sense.hpp.why: a port is only a contract until something implements it; the stub is what proves the shape is implementable

hal/dc_link.hpp.why: a port is only a contract until something implements it; the stub is what proves the shape is implementable

hal/position.hpp.why: a port is only a contract until something implements it; the stub is what proves the shape is implementable

hal/pwm.hpp.why: a port is only a contract until something implements it; the stub is what proves the shape is implementable

api/foc_api.h.why: the C surface is the product path: a capability that is not reachable here is not shipped at all

version.h.why: the one string C and C++ share, on the same path

driver/callback_hal.hpp.why: a reference implementation of a contract: it is the example, so it owes being exercised rather than being documented

driver/scripted_current.hpp.why: a reference implementation of a contract: it is the example, so it owes being exercised rather than being documented

driver/sim_position.hpp.why: a reference implementation of a contract: it is the example, so it owes being exercised rather than being documented

driver/stub_dc_link.hpp.why: a reference implementation of a contract: it is the example, so it owes being exercised rather than being documented

driver/stub_hal.hpp.why: a reference implementation of a contract: it is the example, so it owes being exercised rather than being documented

driver/stub_pwm.hpp.why: a reference implementation of a contract: it is the example, so it owes being exercised rather than being documented

hal/hall.hpp.why: three bits is the whole interface a hall set offers; the decoder and the sequencing rule are ours, reading the pins is the host's

driver/stub_hall.hpp.why: a settable code so the policy can be exercised without a board, and it deliberately does not validate -- an illegal code reaching the policy is the policy's case

core/trace_parse.hpp.why: a host-side reader of the trace channel: the firmware never parses its own ring

comm/frame.hpp.why: a link layer the host drives; the firmware's control path never frames anything

comm/register_map.hpp.why: the protocol's view of the C surface: a host asks, the firmware answers, nothing in the loop calls it
